result.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
result.comment: 6 pages, 1 figure. Trace-driven prototype evaluated on NVIDIA H800
result.summary: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels skip tiles beyond that shape, while graph topology, allocations, layouts, pointers, and launch grids remain fixed; the update transfers only 28 bytes. On one NVIDIA H800, a trace-driven prototype with Qwen2.5-3B dimensions replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, matches the warmed baseline in observed step latency (17.7 vs. 17.8 ms P50), and reduces measured pre-serving graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. Fixed-draft controls show that the benefit comes from avoiding padded payload: the P99 difference from MaxPad is negligible at zero padding waste but reaches an 18.7% reduction at 100% waste. Our evidence establishes a bounded work-shape mechanism for custom kernels, not a production serving system, and is limited to synthetic traces on one GPU.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PolyGraph：为定制 Triton kernel 只捕获一个最大网格的 CUDA Graph，并在每次重放前把激活形状写入显存，让 kernel 跳过形状外的 tile，以适应自适应推测解码中变化的验证宽度 B·d。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于 LLM 服务系统层面的 CUDA Graph 形状管理与投机解码启动开销优化，与 LVR 的视觉状态保留、latent 状态生成与使用、证据获取和停止决策均无实质联系；其「形状自适应」与 latent 推理的动态计算预算只是表面相似，不构成可供核查的方法线索。
